documents.title: Generative AI Guidelines for MSU
documents.summary: ITS guidance on responsible generative AI use focused on data security: only public data in AI tools, vetted and contracted products for confidential data, and compliance with OP 01.12. It says nothing about coursework or academic integrity.
documents.stance_why: The text sets no ban or encouragement of AI; it gives "general guidelines for the responsible use of generative AI" about data and security and defers to existing university policy, so it takes no stance on teaching and learning.

units.why: Scope statement: the document says it gives "general guidelines for the responsible use of generative AI", an institution-level framework with no course focus; P56 fits as the preamble of purpose and scope.
units.anchor: general guidelines for the responsible use of generative AI at Mississippi State University
units.frag_start: This document provides general guidelines
units.frag_end: generative AI at Mississippi State University

units.why: Frames AI tools as "posting data on a public website", a privacy principle that tells users what to assume when using a tool; P50 (protect data) fits better than P56 because the point is data exposure.
units.anchor: AI tools and services should be viewed as posting data on a public website
units.frag_start: AI tools and services should be viewed
units.frag_end: posting data on a public website

units.why: "Only publicly available information ... may be used" in AI tools is a data-use limit binding all users; P50 protects confidential data. It is not P49 because it concerns any non-public data, not course materials specifically.
units.anchor: Only publicly available information
units.frag_start: Only publicly available information (data that
units.frag_end: may be used in generative AI tools and services
units.policy: Only publicly available information (data with no legal or other requirement for confidentiality, integrity, or availability under the Freedom of Information Act) may be used in generative AI tools and services.

units.why: Warns users to "expect these AI tools and services to use input data for its training", a fact about tool data practices supporting the privacy rule; P50 covers "AI tools store prompts".

units.frag_start: Users should expect
units.frag_end: including the derivative use of any data submitted

units.why: Where source information requires authentication, "permission from the respective division VP may be needed" before putting it in AI tools; an approval step for restricted data, coded P50 as data protection.

units.frag_end: information in AI tools and services

units.why: Directs questions about data standards and security to the "Chief Information Security Officer"; it assigns a contact and support route. P50 is the closest home (data security guidance), though it is mainly a referral.
units.anchor: security should be directed to the Chief Information Security Officer
units.frag_start: Questions about university data standards
units.policy: Questions about university data standards and security are directed to the Chief Information Security Officer.

units.why: "Generative AI should be used in accordance with the existing university policies (OP 01.12)" ties AI use to an existing institutional framework, so P56 fits.
units.anchor: Generative AI should be used in accordance with the existing university policies (OP 01.12)
units.frag_start: Follow university policies and procedures
units.policy: Follow university policies and procedures; generative AI should be used in accordance with existing university policies (OP 01.12) and the campus information security program.

units.why: "Understand if informed consent and approval of the data subjects is required" asks users to consider data-subject consent before using AI; coded P50 as personal data protection.
units.anchor: Understand if informed consent and approval of the data subjects is required
units.frag_start: Understand if informed consent

units.why: Users handling proprietary or confidential information "Must use products or services that have undergone a comprehensive security risk review"; this is the vetted-tools rule in P50.
units.anchor: Must use products or services that have undergone a comprehensive security risk review
units.frag_start: Must use products or services that have undergone
units.frag_end: data classification by MSU Chief Information Security Officer
units.policy: For MSU proprietary or confidential information, students, faculty, staff and affiliates must use products or services that have undergone a comprehensive security risk review based on use case and data classification by the MSU Chief Information Security Officer.

units.why: Users handling confidential information "Must use products or services that have a university contract in place" covering training use; a vetted/licensed tool requirement, P50 rather than P65 because it binds users, not institutional review.
units.anchor: have a university contract in place that protects university data
units.frag_start: Must use products or services that have a university
units.policy: For MSU proprietary or confidential information, students, faculty, staff and affiliates must use products or services that have a university contract in place that protects university data and specifically addresses how MSU information will be used by training models and whether it is accessible to external parties.

documents.unit: CITE (Center for Instructional Technology and Excellence)
documents.title: Suggested MSU Generative AI Syllabus Statements
documents.summary: CITE offers three suggested syllabus statements ranging from open use with citation to moderate (instructor-designated assignments, disclosure, detection) to strict (AI use is academic dishonesty). Instructors pick one; the statements are suggestions, not binding rules.
documents.stance_why: The document is a menu of "Option 1: Open", "Option 2: Moderate" and "Option 3: Strict" statements, so it sets no single stance and hands the choice to instructors.

units.why: The CITE document offers three named options (open, moderate, strict) for instructors to adopt; "Suggested ... Syllabus Statements" with graded levels is a tiered scheme, P05.
units.anchor: Option 1: Open Use Guidelines
units.frag_start: Option 1: Open Use Guidelines
units.policy: The suggested syllabus statements are organized as three named levels of AI use: Option 1 Open, Option 2 Moderate, Option 3 Strict.

units.why: Supplying suggested syllabus statements for instructors to choose from leaves the rule to each instructor; P04 captures per-instructor choice, while the tier naming is coded separately as P05.
units.anchor: Suggested Mississippi State University Generative AI Syllabus Statements
units.frag_start: Suggested Mississippi State University
units.policy: Instructors choose among suggested syllabus statements for AI use in their course.

units.why: Option 1 says "students are encouraged to use Generative AI Tools such as ChatGPT to support their work", a default encouragement within that tier; P02.

units.why: Option 1 requires students to "give credit and cite any AI-generated material" under documentation rules; a disclosure/citation duty, P24.
units.anchor: Students must give credit and cite any AI-generated material
units.frag_start: Students must give credit and cite
units.policy: Students must give credit and cite any AI-generated material according to rules of documentation including in-text citations, quotations, and references.

units.why: Option 1 requires the quoted acknowledgement "The author acknowledges the use of [Generative AI Tool Name]", naming tool and purpose; a statement with each submission, P24 (P25 would need prompt/output detail, which is absent).

units.policy: Students must include in assignments a statement acknowledging the use of the named Generative AI tool and the purpose, such as brainstorming, grammatical correction or citation.

units.policy: Students must give credit and cite any AI-generated material according to [APA, MLA, etc.] rules, including in-text citations, quotations, and references.
